The code passed steps 3 and 4; T1 (guard tests and fixtures/browser.js) is closed (handoffs/M1CODE-20261119-01/step-05-test-designer-t1.json). Write the unit files of REQ-111 under app/test/unit/ — public-pages, texts, forbidden-words, theme-contrast, intake, vendored, public-build — each test exactly as section 10 of docs/design/REQ-111-112-public-landing.md names it (ids, what it checks, damaged copies or mutants for every rule, the states and languages it covers), and add their names to UNIT_FILES of app/test/int/node-main.test.js (row 3 of section 11, NM-5) in the same sub-step. Map PP-6 into the test column of row REQ-111/10 (decisions/0124 H5: the test exists; the table is DOC-UPDATER's), run each next-rule row of TX-7 with a stored value that is a language of the build other than ru (H3, M36 named against it), cover decisions/0124 H2 where the design puts it in T2. The goal: cd app && npm run check fully green, no skip, todo or only (the grep of REQ-108 criterion 2 over app/test prints no line, comments included); every rule a test enforces is proved red on a planted damaged copy or mutant in a scratch clone of the working tree state; a test that finds a defect of the built code is a BLOCKED first issue, the code is not edited.

result.summary: T2 is done. `cd app && npm run check` ends with exit 0: prettier, eslint, tsc, check-public, vendored, the picker check of the intake, unit 92 of 92 (the 47 of T1 and 45 new: PP 7, TX 8, FW 8, TC 5, IN 6, VD 4, PB 7), int 36 of 36 (NM-5 now guards 21 unit files), skipped 0, todo 0, fail 0. The grep of REQ-108 criterion 2 over app/test prints no line (exit 1). No test found a defect of the built code: every new test was green on the code as built, so there is no BLOCKED issue and the code was not touched. Seven unit files are new (app/test/unit/public-pages, texts, forbidden-words, theme-contrast, intake, vendored, public-build .test.js), each test named by its id of section 10; app/test/int/node-main.test.js has the seven names in UNIT_FILES and its NM-5 title says 21 (it says 25 after T3); one helper file app/test/fixtures/blank.js (no test) is new, see I2. Proof that every rule is red: 254 mutants and planted copies in a scratch clone of the working tree state (a copy of the tree with its uncommitted T1 files; one edit at a time; the file restored from its saved text, the sha256 of the tree equal before and after each series): 253 red, each in the test or tests expected, 1 not red by nature (IN6b, see I6); all 40 mutants of section 13 that belong to these files are among them (M01-M08, M10, M20-M32, M35-M43, M62-M65, M78, M79, M89-M91; M09 is DM-2 of T3, M33 and M34 are CP-2 of T1, M44 on are T3 and T4). Every damaged copy that a test builds itself (the nine of PP-5, the seven of TX-8, TC-4, IN-5, VD-3, PB-6 a-k, and others) is applied to the same function that passes the real files, so it is red in the run itself. No test was weakened, skipped or deleted. Mapping criterion -> test (Q5): REQ-111 criterion 1 -> PP-1..PP-5 and PP-7; criterion 2 -> TX-1..TX-8; criterion 3 -> FW-1..FW-8; criterion 4 -> TC-1..TC-5; criterion 5 -> IN-1..IN-6 and the step content; criterion 6 -> VD-1..VD-4 and the step vendored; criterion 9 -> PB-1..PB-7 and PP-7; criterion 10 -> PP-6 (decisions/0124 H5: the CSSOM closed list joins the test column of row REQ-111/10 with CP-1..CP-3), the other rows are T1's and T4's. Decisions/0124: H3 (each 'next rule' row of TX-7 - de, RU, Kk, EN, an empty value, <script>, 1 000 characters, ' en', 'en ', ru-RU, en-US, ruru, e - runs with the stored values en and kk of the build and with none; M36 is red in TX-7 by the rows with the stored en; M37 and a stored-value rule that is dropped are red by the same rows); H5 (PP-6 exists, strict as 4.10 writes it, no exception for draw.js); H2 is the demo speaker's avatar redrawn after a theme change on demo.html and is F7 and T4's (LD-4/LD-5, an e2e test): the design puts nothing of it in T2; H1 and H6 are B5's, and PB-6 now holds the shape H1 names (k: a marker-like comment inside a region). The CODE-FIXER's finding SEC L1 (handoffs step-02b, issue I3, FOR_TEST_DESIGNER: the public set refuses every symbolic link before it reads or writes) has its rows in PB-6: six links (a page, the texts module, the texts module as a link to a file that cannot be imported, a folder, examples.html, a page whose markers cannot be paired, two links with the first in name order, one below a folder), the folder itself as a link, and the build into another folder with a relative link in the source (exit 1, the source as it was, no output folder), with the outside targets byte-equal and the copy as it was; mutants: refuseLinks removed, called after the import, not called before the copy, not walking folders, in reverse order - all red. SEC L2 (the questionnaire route, DM-6) is T3's. Quality-bar items: Q7 no secret in any test; Q6 no skip, no turned-off rule, nothing weakened; Q8 and Q11 are not touched by these files (no customer space, no address that a visitor supplies; the demo routes with Q8 and Q10 are T3's int tests); Q9 no SQL; Q10: the build and the lint with a failure input (a texts module that cannot be imported, an unreadable record, a missing file) are tested to give a named refusal and leave the folder as it was; R3 not applicable (decisions/0033).

issues.text: Section 10 (PP-6) says «the eleven allowed writes» green; the closed list of 4.10 names ten: nine in office/view.js (--H, --rw, --dt, --wh, --cx1..--cx4, --you) and one in js/pages/demo.js (--tx), and the served code writes exactly these (13 uses before the review fix of M1, 10 after). PP-6 reads the ten from the files (a map of the nine and the one, equal to the writes found) and its green forms are 16 (each of the ten, a spread-over-lines form, a word in a comment, a block comment with a slash, a regular expression, a string with escaped quotes, a template). The number 'eleven' of the design is a miscount; for DOC-UPDATER.

TX-7 names «the `blank` of import-boundaries.test.js» as the tool to read lang.js after blanking. A test file cannot be imported for it: importing a file with test() calls runs those tests again in the importing file (measured: a b.test.js imported by an a.test.js ran its test as well), so IB-1..IB-4 would run in every file that imports blank and the counts of the design would be wrong. The reader is therefore a small new helper, app/test/fixtures/blank.js (no test in it, as decisions/0124 O10 allowed browser.js), written fresh in the test code and not imported from the tests; T3's OP-2 needs the same and can import it. Its correctness is held by the tests that use it: four mutants of it are red in PP-6, and PP-6 has green forms for each kind it blanks.
Counts after T2: unit 92 (47 + 45), int 36, e2e 0. NPM-5's title still says 10 int files (T3 changes it with INT_FILES, row 2) and NM-5's title says 21 unit files (25 after T3's four, row 3).

Equivalent and non-rule mutants, named so they are not read as missed: (a) in list П the lookahead (?![.,]\\p{Nd}) after 100 is redundant (the next sign must be a space, U+00A0, U+202F, % or a letter anyway): removing it changes no answer, so no test can be red on it (the mutant FW4c, not in the table); (b) IN6b adds one rule to the intake: the step's line then says one rule more and IN-6 reads M from the same file, so it stays green by design (REQ-111 criterion 5 leaves M free; the F2 build says 35, design 4.9 says 32 on the sketch). Both are harmless.

Things the tests do beyond the catalogue, each from the design's own text and none a new requirement: PB-1 compares without letter case and with the white space of the file folded (the stricter reading that F1e of the build left to T2); the TX-7 table runs 13 near forms of the query with the stored values en and kk and 5 mutated copies of lang.js; TX-6 runs 6 mutated copies of text-rules.js on its own corpus; PP-6 reads `.style` as a word in the code, so `draw.js`-like fields called style would be red (the REVIEWER's M1, fixed by the rename to hairdo); VD-3 also asserts that the step leaves the temporary tree unchanged. PB-4 and the git calls need git on the PATH, as VB-4 does.

H2 of decisions/0124 (the demo speaker's canvas[data-avatar] redrawn for the asking desk at each question and after each theme change; LD-4 or LD-5 reads its --sc-chair on demo.html) is assigned by the decision to F7 and T4; none of the seven unit files reads a page in a browser, so there is nothing to cover in T2. The unit part that touches it (drawn theme and the pure theme.js, TC-1 and TC-5) is covered. Passed to T4.

No test of this sub-step caught an error of the code, and no edit of the code is needed. Known and not mine: `cd tools && npm run handoffs-check` prints the one PENDING line of handoffs/M0DOCS-20261117-01/step-05c-test-designer.json.
